editorial:
Imagine being the person who has to call dozens of strangers to ask them about the worst moments of their lives. That is exactly what you see happening here. You follow two smart reporters from the New York Times who are trying to uncover the truth about a powerful movie mogul. It is not a loud action movie, but it feels like a race against time. The vibe is very grounded and professional, showing you the hard work, the long phone calls, and the scary legal threats that come with taking down a giant in the industry.

The acting is great because it feels real, not like a scripted drama. You will love seeing how the two women support each other while dealing with a lot of stress. The pacing is steady, though some might find the middle a bit slow since it is mostly talking. If you enjoy stories about justice and bravery, you should definitely check this out. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for a crisp look, or maybe rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. If you love owning your films, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a solid choice.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with the New York Times finally publishing the massive story. You see the immediate fallout as more women find the courage to speak out, creating a wave of change. It ends by showing how this one article helped start the #MeToo movement globally. There is no big twist, just the satisfying feeling of the truth coming out and the powerful man finally losing his grip on the world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about journalism and fighting for the truth.
